details: Implementation Plan Implementation plan: stuck-states P3a, the producer side of the failure-fingerprint markers (Refs #8291) Planning ref: `orchestrator/project-8291` at `08a5d8d304ee4fd931c882c69c340288d304c5ab`. The integration branch matches (`Integration branch mismatch: false`). Clarification answers: none were needed. This is an orchestrator-managed issue, so the orchestrator auto-answered it. Scope comes from section P3 of `docs/plans/remove-unattended-pipeline-stuck-states-plan.md`. P3 says the plan and clarify failure handlers compute `fingerprint = sha256(phase + failed_step_name + first ::error:: line normalized)[:12]` and append `` to the failure comment they already post, without posting a new comment. The consumer half (P3b) is already on this ref. `evaluate_failure_fingerprint_breaker` and `FAILURE_FINGERPRINT_MARKER_RE` live in `scripts/orchestrate_lib.py` (around lines 3756-3800), and `_failure_fingerprint_breaker_check` lives in `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`. The README section "Stall recovery: failure-signature breaker" already says the markers are "written by the plan and clarify failure handlers", but nothing writes them yet. This plan closes that gap. Scope-mode: Hold Scope Reuse-audit: extends workflow_failure_heal.py (normalize_error_line / _GENERIC_ERROR_RE / single_line) and the jobs-API failed-step lookup in review_autofix_step_assemble_failure_evidence.sh Scope-mode justification: The project plan fixes this phase's scope at two places: the plan and clarify failure-comment steps. `orchestrate_clarify_respond.yml` and `implement.yml` are not in P3's file list, so they stay out. The complete version is small: one pure Python subcommand, about 25 lines of shell in each "Comment on issue failure" step, and tests. It adds no dependency and no new external interface; it only reads two GitHub REST endpoints the repo already uses. Under the §6 priority order (Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed), I chose the complete fail-open version. It includes a self-check that every emitted marker matches the consumer's regex, a parity test against `orchestrate_lib.FAILURE_FINGERPRINT_MARKER_RE`, and an end-to-end test that feeds produced markers into the breaker. A marker-only shortcut without those checks is not enough. ## Automation wiring (§20.E) - **Scripts:** no new script. This extends `scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py` with a subcommand, and edits the existing failure steps of two reusable workflows. - **Entry points:** `.github/workflows/plan.yml` and `.github/workflows/clarify.yml`, step "Comment on issue failure", which runs on `failure() || cancelled()`. Both are triggered through the existing `ai-plan.yml`/`internal-plan.yml` and `ai-clarify.yml`/`internal-clarify.yml` wrappers. The consumer of the markers is already wired: `orchestrate_poll.yml` cron → `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`. - **Supervisor:** none. This rides existing runs. - **DB work:** none, so §12 and §20.D do not apply. - **`docs/scripts-pending-removal.md`:** no entry, because no new script is introduced. ## Files likely to change - `scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py` - `.github/workflows/plan.yml` - `.github/workflows/clarify.yml` - `tests/test_workflow_failure_heal.py` - `README.md` - `agents.d/stuck-states-p3a-fingerprint-markers.md` (new) - `changelog.d/stuck-states-p3a-fingerprint-markers.md` (new) ## Functions or modules to implement 1. **`scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py`: new pure function and subcommand.** - Why this module: it is already staged for both phases. It is in plan.yml's legacy copy list (line 630), clarify.yml's (line 504), and the `clarify)` / `plan)` lists in `scripts/stage_support_for_phase.sh` (lines 95, 103, 118). It also already owns `normalize_error_line` (around line 3226), `_GENERIC_ERROR_RE` (line 3429), `single_line` and `safe_token`. `scripts/orchestrate_lib.py` is not staged for plan or clarify, so the producer cannot import the consumer's regex at runtime. - New constants: - `PHASE_FAILURE_FINGERPRINT_PHASES = ("plan", "clarify")` - `PHASE_FAILURE_FINGERPRINT_MARKER_RE`, a byte-for-byte copy of `orchestrate_lib.FAILURE_FINGERPRINT_MARKER_RE`: `` - `PHASE_FAILURE_FINGERPRINT_NO_ERROR = "no-error-line"` - I grepped for `PHASE_FAILURE_FINGERPRINT`, and none of these names exist anywhere today. - `phase_failure_fingerprint(*, phase, run_id, runner_name, jobs, annotations) -> dict`, pure with no I/O. It returns `{"marker": str, "fp": str, "reason": str, "error_present": bool}`. - Validate `phase` against `PHASE_FAILURE_FINGERPRINT_PHASES`; otherwise `reason=invalid_phase`. - Validate `run_id` with `^[1-9][0-9]{0,19}$`; otherwise `reason=invalid_run_id`. - Find the failed step. `jobs` is the parsed jobs-API object. Pick the first job whose `runner_name` equals `runner_name`, then the first step in that job with `conclusion == "failure"`. This is the same selection as `scripts/review_autofix_step_assemble_failure_evidence.sh` line 9. - If there is no runner match, no failed step, or a non-dict or malformed shape: `reason=step_unknown` and no marker. - Find the first error. `annotations` is the parsed check-run annotations list. Take the first entry with `annotation_level == "failure"` whose `message`, reduced to its first line, does not match `_GENERIC_ERROR_RE`. That regex skips "Process completed with exit code N." and lines ending in "Aborting." - Normalize the message with `normalize_error_line(...)`. If nothing is found or the input is malformed, use `PHASE_FAILURE_FINGERPRINT_NO_ERROR`. - Compute `fp = sha256("|".join([phase, single_line(step_name, 200).lower(), normalized_error[:SIGNATURE_CHAR_LIMIT]]).encode()).hexdigest()[:12]`. - Build `marker = f""`. Emit it only if `PHASE_FAILURE_FINGERPRINT_MARKER_RE.fullmatch(marker)`; otherwise `reason=marker_invalid`. - `_cmd_phase_failure_fingerprint(args)`, registered as `phase-failure-fingerprint`. - Arguments: `--phase` (choices plan/clarify), `--run-id`, `--runner-name`, `--jobs-json FILE`, `--annotations-json FILE` (optional, missing or unreadable is treated as `[]`). - It reads the files and fails open on `OSError` or `json.JSONDecodeError` (`reason=jobs_unavailable`). - It prints `marker=…`, `fp=…`, `error_present=0|1`, `reason=…`, one per line, and always exits 0. - It never prints the step name or the error text, so nothing new is logged that could hold a secret. 2. **`.github/workflows/plan.yml`, step "Comment on issue failure" (around lines 3442-3457).** - Keep the `name:` and `if:`. - Add these env entries: - `STALL_FINGERPRINT_BREAKER_ENABLED: ${{ vars.STALL_FINGERPRINT_BREAKER_ENABLED || 'true' }}`, which reuses P3b's existing kill switch; no new env var. - `FP_JOB_STATUS: ${{ job.status }}`, `FP_RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}`, `FP_RUN_ATTEMPT: ${{ github.run_attempt }}`, `FP_REPOSITORY: ${{ github.repository }}` - Before the existing `gh_retry gh api …/comments` call, add a fail-open block. Every command uses `|| true`, so the comment is always posted. - Set `FP_MARKER_SUFFIX=""`. - Only when `FP_JOB_STATUS == failure`, `STALL_FINGERPRINT_BREAKER_ENABLED == true`, and `"${SUPPORT_SCRIPTS_DIR:-scripts}/workflow_failure_heal.py"` is a regular file: 1. `gh_retry gh api "repos/${FP_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/${FP_RUN_ID}/attempts/${FP_RUN_ATTEMPT:-1}/jobs?per_page=100"`, written to `"${RUNNER_TEMP}/phase_fp_jobs.json"`. 2. jq extracts `[.jobs[] | select(.runner_name == env.RUNNER_NAME) | .id][0] // empty`; keep it only if it matches `^[1-9][0-9]*$`. 3. If the id is valid: `gh_retry gh api "repos/${FP_REPOSITORY}/check-runs/${job_id}/annotations?per_page=50"`, written to `"${RUNNER_TEMP}/phase_fp_annotations.json"`. 4. `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 "${SUPPORT_SCRIPTS_DIR:-scripts}/workflow_failure_heal.py" phase-failure-fingerprint --phase plan --run-id "${FP_RUN_ID}" --runner-name "${RUNNER_NAME}" --jobs-json … --annotations-json …` 5. Parse `marker=`. Re-check it against a bash `[[ =~ ]]` copy of the regex and set `FP_MARKER_SUFFIX=$'\n\n'"${marker}"`. - Echo `PHASE_FAILURE_FINGERPRINT phase=plan issue=${ISSUE_NUMBER} run=${FP_RUN_ID} outcome=emitted|skipped [fp=] [reason=] error_line=0|1`. - Append `${FP_MARKER_SUFFIX}` to the existing `-f body=` string after `${PLAN_CANCELLED_SUFFIX}`, so the marker is the last line. The body still starts with `AI planning workflow failed.`, which `PHASE_FAILURE_COMMENT_PREFIXES["plan"]` uses with `startswith`, so the heal streak counter is unaffected. - Above the `gh api` calls, add a §14 comment covering: - Which calls were audited: none in this failure path return job steps or annotations. - API cost: 2 REST calls only on a failed run, 0 when cancelled or disabled. - Fail-open behaviour. - The source of the pattern: `review_autofix_step_assemble_failure_evidence.sh`. 3. **`.github/workflows/clarify.yml`, step "Comment on issue failure" (around lines 2285-2299).** Same block with `--phase clarify` and the log line's `phase=clarify`. - Append the suffix to the `REASON` body, so the body still starts with `AI clarification workflow failed for `. - The cancelled path (`…was cancelled/timed out…`) never gets a marker. - The step's existing `if:` (which excludes `CLAUDE_CAPACITY_WAIT`) stays unchanged. ## Deferred scope (None.
